security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, reference links, generic database variables, and RAG terminology. Two semantic concerns remain in the examples: prompt/user logging without redaction and agent tool execution without explicit guardrails. No prompt injection attempt or malicious exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Prompt logging can expose user data.
remediation.suggestion: Redact prompts and user identifiers before logging. Add retention limits, access controls, and clear guidance for handling sensitive input.

remediation.issue: Agent tool execution examples omit security guardrails.
remediation.suggestion: Show allowlisted tools, strict argument schemas, permission checks, sandboxing, and prompt-injection defenses around every tool call.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Data Logging Without Redaction
semantic_findings.description: The LLMLogger example logs prompt fragments and user_id into application logs. This can expose sensitive user content if copied into production without redaction or retention controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly includes data["prompt"][:500] and user_id in log_entry before logging. It is an illustrative pattern, not proof of deployed exfiltration.

semantic_findings.title: Agent Tool Execution Lacks Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: The agent examples parse model output and pass tool calls to execution helpers without showing authorization, schema validation, or sandboxing. Applications copying this pattern could expose tools to prompt injection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples execute parsed or model-provided tool calls, and no guardrail layer is shown. Confidence is moderate because the snippets are conceptual documentation.

content.value_statement: LLM applications can fail without clear patterns for retrieval, agents, prompts, and monitoring. This skill gives practical templates for RAG, agents, prompt workflows, and LLMOps.
actual_capabilities: Explains RAG ingestion, chunking, embedding, retrieval, and generation stages.
Compares vector database options and embedding model choices.
Shows ReAct, function calling, plan-and-execute, and multi-agent patterns.
Provides prompt template, versioning, A/B testing, and chaining patterns.
Lists LLMOps metrics, tracing ideas, evaluation checks, caching, retries, and fallbacks.
limitations: Examples are illustrative and are not a complete runnable framework.
It does not include provider-specific authentication setup or deployment scripts.
Some model names, pricing, and ecosystem links may become outdated.
Security controls are discussed indirectly and should be added before production.

use_cases.title: Plan a RAG Knowledge Assistant
use_cases.description: Choose chunking, embedding, retrieval, prompting, and citation patterns for a grounded assistant.

use_cases.title: Select an Agent Architecture
use_cases.description: Compare ReAct, function calling, plan-and-execute, and multi-agent designs for a task.

use_cases.title: Define LLMOps Monitoring
use_cases.description: Set metrics for latency, quality, cost, reliability, evaluation, retries, caching, and fallbacks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a RAG Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the llm-app-patterns skill to recommend a RAG design for a support knowledge base. Include ingestion, retrieval, and generation choices.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Agent Architectures
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the llm-app-patterns skill to compare ReAct, function calling, plan-and-execute, and multi-agent designs for my workflow. List tradeoffs and risks.

prompt_templates.title: Design LLMOps Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the llm-app-patterns skill to define monitoring metrics for an LLM feature. Cover quality, cost, latency, reliability, and alerting.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Production LLM Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the llm-app-patterns skill to review this LLM architecture for retrieval quality, tool safety, observability, caching, rate limits, and fallback behavior.

output_examples.input: Design a RAG chatbot for internal policies.
output_examples.output: A RAG plan with document-aware chunking, hybrid retrieval, grounded generation, citations, and evaluation metrics.

output_examples.input: Select an agent pattern for a support workflow.
output_examples.output: A comparison of function calling and ReAct, with a recommendation based on tool count, validation needs, and operational risk.
A monitoring plan covering latency percentiles, error rate, hallucination checks, cost tracking, retries, caching, and fallback model rules.

best_practices: Treat all examples as starting points and add security controls before production.
Match architecture complexity to the task, cost limits, and operational maturity.
Measure quality, latency, cost, and safety before expanding an LLM feature.
anti_patterns: Copying agent tool execution examples without allowlists or argument validation.
Logging prompts or user identifiers without redaction, retention limits, and access controls.
Choosing multi-agent designs when a simple RAG or function-calling flow is enough.

faq.question: Does this skill run code or install packages?
faq.answer: No. It is a Markdown guide with illustrative Python patterns.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The content is text guidance that these tools can apply during design work.

faq.question: Does it replace a full LLM framework?
faq.answer: No. It explains patterns, but implementation details still depend on your stack.

faq.question: What LLM application areas does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers RAG, agents, prompt workflows, observability, evaluation, caching, retry, and fallback patterns.

faq.question: What security work is still needed?
faq.answer: Add input validation, tool authorization, secret handling, prompt redaction, logging controls, and prompt-injection defenses.

faq.question: Is the pricing information guaranteed current?
faq.answer: No. Verify model pricing and vendor capabilities before making cost decisions.
